About matching & export

Signature protection: always on. PDFs with detected digital signatures open in view-only mode. Download returns the exact uploaded file unchanged; signed and view-only documents skip the export choice entirely. Hash original fingerprints those exact uploaded bytes too. Password-protected PDFs can be unlocked in this browser after the password is accepted; only a working copy is decrypted. This editor does not verify certificate trust or signature validity.

Font names and sizes come from the PDF. Bold and italic are inferred from font names; underline and paragraph structure are not reliably encoded.

The editor reuses the PDF's embedded font program, so characters used elsewhere in the document are available here too. Subset fonts can still lack characters that never appear; load the full TTF/OTF for those.

One typography model: font size, X/Y baseline, letter spacing, word spacing, stroke weight and line height are PDF points rounded to 0.001 pt. The preview, the in-place editor and the native export use the same glyph advances with kerning and ligatures disabled, so a fraction of a point is never added or lost between them. Original fill, stroke, fill+stroke paint modes, stroke colors and text rise are preserved.

Exports preserve native text, graphics and existing images. Edited text stays selectable; pages are never converted to images.

Export choice: Export PDF asks for a regular export or an AES-256 password-protected copy. Encryption requires an open password of at least 8 characters plus confirmation, with an optional different owner password. The normal native export is created first, then those bytes are encrypted in this browser. Passwords are used only for that export, cleared afterwards, and never uploaded or saved.

Watermarks and artwork remain in their original PDF structure. Check the export before sharing. Edits can be detected and may invalidate signatures.

Export size depends on the original content and any fonts you add. Previously rasterized PDFs remain images; reopen the original PDF to keep its text.

Sign a new copy

Your certificate and password stay in this browser. Signing adds a record page identifying the new signer. Existing signed PDFs remain protected.

Choose a certificate to see the signing identity.

RSA 2048+ only. Certificate trust and revocation are not checked. Signing time uses your device clock; no trusted timestamp is included.

Encrypt a PDF copy

Choose any unencrypted PDF; this works independently of the document open in the editor. Password protection is applied in this browser, with AES-256 or RC4 128-bit. This standalone action is separate from the Export PDF choice in the editor and does not depend on the open document. Existing digital signatures cannot be preserved in a rewritten file, so signed PDFs are refused.

RC4 128-bit is the older scheme; some bank and archive systems cannot open AES-256. It is weaker, so it is only offered for files that must be read by one of them. It needs no secure context.

When supplied, only this JSON’s fields become the encrypted PDF’s native Info/XMP metadata: omitted original Info fields and XMP are removed, and the JSON file is not attached. Use the metadata JSON downloaded from this app, a file metadata report such as {"file":{"name":"statement.pdf","sizeBytes":583255,"hashes":{"SHA-256":"…"}},"metadata":{"version":"1.4","pages":15,"Producer":"openhtmltopdf.com","CreationDate":"D:…"}} (only its real PDF metadata such as Producer/CreationDate is written; file names, sizes, hashes and version details are ignored), a flat object such as {"Title":"New title","Author":"Name","Custom":{"Project":"123"}}, or {"info":{"Title":"New title"},"xmp":{"raw":"...XMP XML..."}}. Leave it empty to retain the source PDF’s existing native metadata. PDF structure properties such as page count, encryption and signatures cannot be set from JSON. Info values must be text, a number, a boolean or a PDF name object such as {"name":"False"}; lists are joined for the standard text fields. Nested objects and arrays cannot be stored in PDF Info. In a flat JSON, every top-level key except xmp/XMP and Custom is treated as an Info field, so remove unrelated keys such as file. If a value is unsupported, nothing is downloaded; fix the JSON or use Encrypt without metadata to keep the PDF’s existing metadata. Passwords are not stored or sent anywhere. Use HTTPS or localhost for AES-256.

This preview is embedded in another page, and some browsers block automatic downloads inside embedded frames. After encrypting, if no file appears, use Save again in the download panel or Open app in new tab, then repeat the encryption there.

Metadata JSON can’t be used

PDF Info is a flat dictionary and can only store text, numbers, booleans or PDF names. The JSON file itself is never attached. Without a usable JSON, the encrypted copy keeps the PDF’s existing native Info/XMP metadata.

Export PDF

The native export is created first in this browser, including your edits and any loaded metadata replacement. Choose whether the downloaded copy should be a regular PDF or password protected with AES-256 or RC4 128-bit.

Export type

Passwords stay in this browser and are used only for this export. They are not uploaded, stored or written into the PDF, and they cannot be recovered if lost.

The standalone Encrypt PDF action above remains separate and does not depend on the open document.

Source PDF metadata

The Info fields below are native metadata from the opened PDF; calculated properties such as PDF version are excluded. Without a replacement file, edited exports retain its Info/XMP and attach nothing. If you choose a JSON replacement below, its supported fields become the PDF's native Info/XMP metadata instead; no new JSON attachment is added. This record does not validate a signature.

Open a PDF to inspect its metadata.

Use a JSON object such as {"Title":"Updated title","Author":"Name","Custom":{"Project":"123"}}, a metadata JSON downloaded here, or or a file metadata report with "file"/"metadata" objects (only its real PDF fields are applied; file names, hashes and structure are ignored, so the export carries no source descriptors). For XMP, include "xmp":{"raw":"...XML..."}. Only supplied Info/XMP fields remain: missing original fields and XMP are removed. PDF structure (pages, encryption, signatures) cannot be replaced by metadata. This is not a redaction of page-level metadata or existing attachments. The new export has different bytes and hashes, even without text edits. Signed PDFs stay view-only; password-protected PDFs are unlocked in-browser when the accepted password can be safely decrypted.

No metadata replacement loaded. The source PDF’s native Info/XMP is retained.

Document fonts

Every page's font resources are read when the PDF opens. A typeface whose embedded program sits on page 1 is offered for text on every page: the editor reuses that program for the preview and the native export instead of substituting a browser font, even when a later page's own font resource carries no program.

Open a PDF to inspect its fonts.

Open a PDF to inspect its fonts.

Detected document fonts appear in Available font with the page that supplied the program. Choose one, then Apply changes. Characters missing from the embedded subset still need the full TTF/OTF. Nothing is uploaded.

Statement check

Every page is read and each transaction row is checked the way a reader checks it: the running balance must follow from the amounts, dates must not go backwards, and a narration code must keep the direction it uses everywhere else in the statement.

Open a statement to check its arithmetic.

Open a statement PDF, then choose Statement check.

Fix balances & remarks rewrites only the balance cells that no longer follow from the amounts, using the amounts already in the document and the same currency, separators and Dr/Cr style. It also changes a remarks code that contradicts its row's direction (UPIAR on a credit row) to the code this statement uses for that direction. Undo restores the previous text. Nothing is uploaded or saved.

File identifier (/ID)

A PDF trailer can carry two byte strings: the permanent identifier created with the file and the changing identifier rewritten whenever the file is saved. Editors and decryptors often replace or re-encode them, which makes file-identity checks report that the PDF changed. This app captures the pair from the PDF you opened, before any in-browser decryption, and writes it back into the export.

Open a PDF to inspect its file identifier.

Use this when the identifier was already lost — for example, reopen an earlier export and choose the original file here, then export again. The selected PDF is only read for its trailer /ID; nothing is uploaded, and no other content is copied. Both values are written exactly as they appear, including literal or hexadecimal encoding. Text edits, metadata replacement and encryption change the file bytes and hashes regardless, so this restores the identifier, not the original fingerprint.

Open a PDF to inspect its file identifier.

File fingerprints

SHA-256 and SHA-512 identify exact file bytes. A hash alone does not prove issuer identity. Hash original always fingerprints the exact uploaded bytes, even when an unlocked working copy is being edited. The current export includes applied edits and any uploaded metadata replacement.

Choose which file to fingerprint.
